slot.brief: Show reaction scheme in figure: aldehyde lacking α-H with concentrated NaOH giving alcohol + salt; identify the reaction and products.

stem: As shown in the figure, an aldehyde is treated with concentrated aqueous $\text{NaOH}$. Which reaction and product pair are represented?

verdicts.working: 4-Methoxybenzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen, so concentrated aqueous NaOH gives a Cannizzaro disproportionation: 4-methoxybenzyl alcohol and sodium 4-methoxybenzoate.

working:
4-Methoxybenzaldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogen.
$2\,\text{ArCHO}+\text{NaOH}\rightarrow\text{ArCH}_2\text{OH}+\text{ArCOONa}$.
This disproportionation is the Cannizzaro reaction.

Independent check: 4-Methoxybenzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen, so concentrated aqueous NaOH gives a Cannizzaro disproportionation: 4-methoxybenzyl alcohol and sodium 4-methoxybenzoate.
solution:
4-Methoxybenzaldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogen, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction in concentrated aqueous NaOH.
$$2\,\text{ArCHO}+\text{NaOH}\rightarrow\text{ArCH}_2\text{OH}+\text{ArCOONa}$$
The products are 4-methoxybenzyl alcohol and sodium 4-methoxybenzoate.
